title: Set a soda can in a seat-back fold-down cup holder: fold down its tray, swing out its ring, set the can in upright
instruction: Put the can of soda in the seat-back cup holder: fold down its tray, swing out its ring, and set the can upright through the ring onto the tray, then let go.
context: Most people have set a drink in a fold-down cup holder: on the back of a car or van seat, in a minivan door, or on a cinema or stadium seat. North American cinemas alone sold about 760 to 780 million tickets in 2025. The US fleet is about 289 million light vehicles (2025). This holder stows flat: its tray stands folded up over its ring. A hand folds the tray down to its stop, then swings the ring up and out to its stop, and a full 12 oz can is lowered through a ring only about 4 mm wider than the can until it stands on the tray. A can lowered at an angle catches the rim and tips; one let go above the ring drops onto the tray. The task ends with both parts open and the can standing upright on the tray inside the ring, both hands clear.
setup: Metres; x forward, y to the robot's left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305); heights above the bench top. (1) Seat-back panel section, fixed: a rigid upholstered-look board 0.45 wide (y) x 0.40 tall x 0.05 thick, standing on the bench, its face at x = 0.360, centred on y = 0 (estimate of a seat back's lower section; a real holder sits 0.6 to 0.7 above the floor, lowered here to bench height for reach, at true scale). (2) a fold-up drink holder (marine type, here modelled to one such unit), black ABS, true size, screwed to the panel's face: a 98 x 95 x 4 mm plate with two folding parts on their own pivots. A ring, 70 mm inside (holds drinks up to 2-3/4 in) and 80 mm outside, band 8 mm tall, on two side arms pivoted along y at the plate's top corners (pivot line at x = 0.338, 0.16 up). A tray, 72 deep x 84 wide, 3 mm floor and 7 mm lips on its front and sides, hinged along y at the plate's bottom (hinge line at x = 0.330, 0.076 up). Both start stowed: the ring hanging flat in front of the plate, the tray folded up over it (33 mm deep in all). Open, each stands level at a hard stop: the ring's centre at (0.296, 0), its top face 0.16 up, 84 mm over the tray floor. No spring or detent; joint damping (0.05 N m s/rad, estimate) holds each where it is put. (3) A 12 oz / 355 ml aluminium soda can, 66 mm x 122.2 mm, 0.37 kg, free, rigid, standing on a 10 cm square mat, 2 mm thick, centred at (0.22, -0.17). Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Reset: lift the can out and back onto its mat, fold the ring down and the tray up; about 30 s. Real trial: the same holder screwed to an upright board, a phone level app on the can, a phone filming the side.
scoring: Read from the state at the end; only the voids latch. 0.33: the tray and the ring each within 10 degrees of fully open. 0.67: also the can inside the ring, its axis within 10 degrees of vertical and of the ring's axis, crossing the ring's top face within 3 mm of its centre, its base 3 mm or more below that face. 1.0: also its base within 2 mm of the tray floor, the can still, every part of both grippers 50 mm or more from the can and the holder, for 2 s running. Void (0): once off its mat, the can tilts past 30 degrees or moves down faster than 0.3 m/s, held or falling (a free drop of about 5 mm); the speed check is simulation only, a real trial applies the tilt check. Real trial: both parts against their stops, a phone level under 10 degrees (also void past 30 degrees once off its mat), the can's base on the tray floor, nothing touching the can for 2 s, and a void if the fingers open with the can top over 5 mm above its seated height (a tape mark on the board, read in the side film).
fidelity: Rigid bodies at the sizes in setup; band, lip and pivot offsets are estimates read from the maker's photo and drawing. The ring and the tray are independent links with hard stops and no spring or detent (none published); damping holds each where put, their weight left out. They collide with each other (the stowed tray blocks the ring), not with the plate. The stowed ring stands 10 mm off the plate (real depth 24 mm). The can is one rigid body, no fluid. The demo reads the can's pose.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (hit the 1,200-step limit). Demo: 1.0 (both arms, 780 steps, 39.0 s, GPU). One arm alone (open tray and ring, set the can) 1.0; holder opened only 0.33; ring before tray 0 (blocked); can kept hold of 0.67; can on the bench beside 0.33; let go 35 mm over the ring 0 (drop); nothing 0.
